prerequisites: Vector analysis, differential and integral calculus of several variables, curve and surface integrals, ordinary differential equations.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a deeper understanding of the concepts and most important technical applications of fluid mechanics.
Imparting a physical understanding of the fundamentals of fluid mechanics.
Imparting knowledge for solving simple problems using simplifying assumptions.
Present concepts and most important technical applications of fluid mechanics thoroughly.
Precisely explain the physical fundamentals of fluid mechanics.
Solve simple problems appropriately using simplifying assumptions.
Consistently present the fundamentals of statics and properties of a fluid.
Reliably calculate forces on a sphere in a flow.
Analyze pipe flows under given boundary conditions.
Represent continuity and Navier-Stokes equations in appropriate form.
Compare Couette, Poiseuille, and Couette-Poiseuille flows regarding their characteristic values.
Correctly apply macroscopic balance equations to one-dimensional systems.
Calculate pump power as well as local and distributed pressure losses in pipelines.
Precisely formulate communication channels and responsibilities in a team.
Present work results appropriately and structured for the audience.
Conduct meetings and short status updates in a goal-oriented manner.
Systematically plan work processes in projects.
Critically compare information from different sources.
Methodically investigate risks, assumptions, and boundary conditions in technical projects.
Efficiently use digital tools for research, analysis, and documentation.

syllabus_topics: Statics and definition of fluid properties
Forces on a sphere in a flow
Basic equations of a viscous flow: Continuity and Navier-Stokes equations
Canonical flows: Couette, Poiseuille and Couette-Poiseuille flow
Macroscopic balance equations: Continuity equation, momentum and Bernoulli equation and application to one-dimensional systems
Pipelines and fluid transport: Pump power and pressure drop (local and distributed)
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical fundamentals and applications

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with calculation examples and theory questions

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written exam comprising calculation examples and theory questions. Specific modalities regarding other forms of performance control (regular homework, class participation, tests) are to be announced in the information system for studies and teaching before the start of the semester.
